description: Composite figure of four line plots, all flow-stress curves: stress (MPa) versus true strain (0-0.9, ticks every 0.1), predicted by a 3D cellular automaton (CA) model for low-alloy steel and compared with experiment. In every panel a black solid line labelled "Experimental" and a black dashed line with open circles labelled "Simulated (3D CA)" give the reference condition, while magenta and blue curves give two two-stage (transient) histories distinguished by the strain at which the transient is imposed (0.2 or 0.4 strain). (a) header "Temperature: 950°C", strain rate stepped up "0.01s⁻¹-0.1s⁻¹"; (b) "Temperature: 950°C", rate stepped down "0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹"; (c) header "Strain rate: 0.01s⁻¹", temperature stepped down "1050°C-950°C" (y axis 45-90 MPa); (d) "Strain rate: 0.01s⁻¹", temperature stepped up "950°C-1050°C". Dashed curves labelled "0.1s⁻¹"/"0.01s⁻¹" (a,b) and "950°C"/"1050°C" (c,d) are constant-condition curves. Transiently increasing Z_p (higher rate, lower temperature) produces an abrupt stress rise, a clear peak and subsequent softening; transiently decreasing Z_p produces an abrupt stress drop to a low plateau. The CA simulation reproduces the experimental transient stress response.

subfigures.description: Flow stress vs true strain at Temperature 950°C. Magenta curve "0.01s⁻¹-0.1s⁻¹(0.2 strain)" rises along the base curve then steps abruptly upward at true strain ≈0.2 to a plateau near 105-108 MPa; blue curve "0.01s⁻¹-0.1s⁻¹(0.4 strain)" steps upward at ≈0.4. Solid black "Experimental" peaks near 85 MPa at ≈0.2 strain then declines. Dashed curves labelled "0.1s⁻¹" (upper, peaking just below the 120 MPa gridline) and "0.01s⁻¹" (lower) with open circles are the Simulated (3D CA) constant-condition results.

Flow stress vs true strain at Temperature 950°C, strain rate stepped down. Magenta "0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹(0.2 strain)" peaks above 110 MPa near strain 0.2 then drops sharply to ≈75 MPa; blue "0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹(0.4 strain)" holds the high level and drops abruptly at ≈0.4. Dashed reference curves labelled "0.1s⁻¹" (upper) and "0.01s⁻¹" (lower, coinciding with the Experimental/Simulated base curve).

Flow stress vs true strain at Strain rate: 0.01s⁻¹, temperature stepped down. Y axis 45-90 MPa. Magenta "1050°C-950°C(0.2 strain)" rises to ≈60 MPa near strain 0.15, steps up at ≈0.2 to ≈70 MPa; blue "1050°C-950°C(0.4 strain)" steps up at ≈0.4. Dashed constant-condition curves labelled "950°C" (upper) and "1050°C" (lower, near the experimental curve).

Flow stress vs true strain at Strain rate: 0.01s⁻¹, temperature stepped up. Magenta "950°C-1050°C(0.2 strain)" peaks near 85 MPa at strain ≈0.2 then drops to ≈55 MPa; blue "950°C-1050°C(0.4 strain)" drops abruptly at ≈0.4. Dashed curves labelled "950°C" (upper) and "1050°C" (lower).

observations.observation: All four panels plot flow stress in MPa against true strain from 0 to 0.9 with tick marks every 0.1; panel (a) and (b) span roughly 55-120 MPa and panels (c) and (d) 45-90 MPa.
Every panel carries the same legend: a solid black line labelled "Experimental" and a dashed black line with open circles labelled "Simulated (3D CA)".
Panel (a) header reads "Temperature: 950°C" and its legend entries are "0.01s⁻¹-0.1s⁻¹(0.2 strain)" (magenta) and "0.01s⁻¹-0.1s⁻¹(0.4 strain)" (blue).
Panel (b) header reads "Temperature: 950°C" with legend entries "0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹(0.2 strain)" (magenta) and "0.1s⁻¹-0.01s⁻¹(0.4 strain)" (blue).

Panels (c) and (d) both have the header "Strain rate: 0.01s⁻¹"; (c) legend entries are "1050°C-950°C(0.2 strain)" and "1050°C-950°C(0.4 strain)", and (d) entries are "950°C-1050°C(0.2 strain)" and "950°C-1050°C(0.4 strain)".
Dashed reference curves are annotated "0.1s⁻¹" (upper) and "0.01s⁻¹" (lower) in panels (a) and (b), and "950°C" (upper) and "1050°C" (lower) in panels (c) and (d).

In panel (a) the transient strain-rate increase produces an abrupt upward step in the magenta curve at true strain ≈0.2 and in the blue curve at ≈0.4, each followed by a plateau near 105 MPa and mild softening.

In panel (b) the transient strain-rate decrease produces an abrupt downward step: the magenta curve drops from above 105 MPa to a ≈75 MPa plateau at strain ≈0.2, and the blue curve drops to a ≈70 MPa plateau at ≈0.4.

In panels (c) and (d) the temperature transient has the opposite sign to the strain-rate transient: lowering temperature to 950°C (c) steps the stress upward, raising it to 1050°C (d) steps the stress downward, consistent with Z_p increasing when strain rate rises or temperature falls.
The dashed curve labelled "0.1s⁻¹" in panel (a) peaks just below the 120 MPa gridline at a true strain between 0.2 and 0.3, the highest stress level shown in the figure.
The caption states the panels show evolutions of flow stress with transient variations in strain rate and temperature at different ε_I predicted by 3D CA models, at T = 950 °C for (a) and (b).
The citing text states the CA model effectively described the peak stress and subsequent stress decline in the second stage after transiently increasing Z_p in Fig. 13a and 13c.
The citing text states the predicted reduction velocity of flow stress agreed better with experimental results than Model 2 after transiently decreasing Z_p in Figs. 8d, 9d, 13b and 13d.
The citing text states Z_p (Eq. 6) was used to characterise the combined effect of strain rate and temperature on the microstructure during hot deformation.
